name: Jellyfin Graveyard Analytics
description: Manage your server's afterlife. Identify lifeless media, condemn dead weight to The Chapel, and track your active Visitors.
overview: Advanced storage reclamation and user analytics.

versions.changelog: Makes the optional "Leaving Soon" home screen row look native. It previously sat flush against the page edge while every other row was indented, with undersized posters and a stray link below the section. It now uses the web client's own section and card markup, so spacing, sizing, hover and focus match the rest of the home screen.

Fixes the public "Leaving Soon: The Chapel" collection being empty. Condemning an item that already carried the tag never added it to the collection, so anything condemned by an earlier version was invisible to viewers. Condemning is idempotent now, and a Sync collection button on the Chapel tab adds everything already tagged. Also fixes the optional home screen row never appearing after a slow load or a login.

Adds an optional "Leaving Soon" row to the home screen listing what is in The Chapel — off by default, and hidden while The Chapel is empty. The Chapel collection also stops telling viewers that a deletion deadline exists: nothing expires, and Last Rites remains a deliberate act by the server owner.

Fixes the Guestbook failing on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and newer, where an API change made it error out. Also: stored XSS and webhook authentication fixes; Plays, Time Played and Reach now reconcile; a rebuilt dashboard with loading, empty and error states; cached aggregates instead of a library walk per row; and a test suite. Minimum server is 10.11.6.
The Chapel Update: Automated collection branding, thematic iconography, and .NET 9 performance optimizations.
Initial Release: Opening the gates to Graveyard Analytics v1.0.
